## [0.18.0] - 2026-08-16

The **OpenAPI release**. v0.17.0 could read a spec and make requests out of it; the document was then thrown away, so nothing downstream knew a contract existed. A collection now *binds* the document it answers to, every request remembers which operation it is, and that identity is what the rest of the release is built on: re-fetch and diff the spec, apply the diff selectively in one transaction, export the collection back out as a document, and judge what came back against the schemas the spec declares - in design mode, in a collection run and over a load run's samples - beside a coverage block saying which of the contract a run actually exercised. Streams grow the other half they were missing (a load run may now consume `text/event-stream`, with events on its sampled captures), a single Send can carry one data row, and a live response can be saved as an example. The bulk of the change is new TypeScript in the app, with the validator, the coverage tally and the streaming load path landing engine-side.

### Added

- **A collection binds the spec it came from, and every request knows its operation.** An OpenAPI import now stores the document verbatim in a new `spec_documents` table with an engine-computed hash, binds it to the root collection, and stamps each request with the operation it is (`operationId` when declared, plus the method and the *templated* path). A document is bound rather than owned - several collections may bind one, so nothing cascades to it and deleting a spec that a collection still holds is a 409 naming the binder. There is no `PUT /specs/:id` on purpose: a changed document is a new one, because rewriting in place would invalidate the hash every run of every bound collection was stamped with. A Spec tab shows the binding, unbinds it, and binds a collection that was never imported from a spec by matching operations to existing requests on method and path shape, disclosing the counts on both sides before anything is written.
- **Sync: re-fetch a bound spec, see exactly what moved, apply only what you tick.** The Spec tab re-reads the document from the origin the binding stored and reports the three buckets - added, changed, removed - as a checklist, with "up to date" meaning byte equality against the stored document rather than a second opinion computed in the renderer. An operation is followed by its `operationId` first and its path shape second, so a path moved under a stable id and an id moved under a stable path each stay one operation, while both-moved is disclosed as a removal plus an addition rather than guessed at. A field you edited yourself is flagged three-way and is never overwritten unless you tick it, and a deletion is never a default. Applying sends one `POST /specs/sync` that the engine performs as a single transaction over the document, the binding and the created, updated and deleted requests; the bound subtree is the boundary, so the route cannot become a way to delete an arbitrary row by id. On an update, only `origin="import"` examples are replaced - examples you saved survive untouched and keep their position, which is what a mock server answers with.
- **Importing a document a collection is already bound to offers Sync.** It used to make a second collection from scratch, without the bound one's operation identities, saved examples or coverage history, and with nothing anywhere saying the first existed. Import now looks the document up before it writes anything, by stored `source_url` or by the bytes, and names the collection it found. Import anyway is still there beside it: a second copy of a spec is a real thing to want, so this is a fork and never a block.
- **Response schema validation, on all three execution paths.** The app extracts what a document declares each response looks like and translates it out of OpenAPI's dialect rather than forwarding it - `nullable: true` and draft-04's boolean `exclusiveMinimum` mean something else under draft-07, and a wrong verdict is worse than none. The engine matches a response to one of those schemas by status pattern and media type and validates it: a chip in the status band and the detail in the Tests tab for a single send, a per-step verdict on collection runs (with an opt-in `failOnSchemaError` that fails only a step which passed everything else), and a deferred walk of the sample reservoirs for load runs. Keywords a draft-07 validator cannot evaluate are counted and named, so nothing is reported clean because part of its contract went unread, and a collection bound to no document shows nothing at all - never judged and judged-and-passed are different answers.
- **Contract coverage on a run report.** "14 of 18 operations covered, every declared 2xx seen, three declared 4xxs never triggered", as a first-class block in the history Overview, the collection run view and a one-line last-run summary on the Spec tab. Every number is exact rather than derived from the bounded results reservoir, counted as each request is sent and each response arrives, and a status hits the most specific pattern that covers it. The index is read once when the plan resolves, so a sync landing mid-run cannot move a run onto a contract it never ran against; a binding whose hash no longer matches yields no block rather than a measurement against the wrong document.
- **Export a collection back out as an OpenAPI document.** A bound collection's stored document is *patched*, never rebuilt - operations nothing claims are removed, a declared parameter whose row carries a value gets it as an `example`, stored examples become response examples, and everything Vayu does not model is carried through by not being visited. A free-form collection gets a skeleton the dialog calls a starting point, with nothing inferred: no schema that was not read off an example body, no `required` from a row's toggle, no response for a status nobody saved. A request with no operation identity is never added to a bound document - the contract never described it - and is counted and named instead.
- **External `$ref`s resolve before parse.** A `$ref` naming another file was walked as a `#/` pointer, landed on `undefined`, and imported the operation as though the spec had documented nothing: an empty body stub, a missing parameter, and no entry in the skip tally to say so. Referenced documents are now fetched or read from beside the picked file, inlined under a root `x-vayu-bundled` key and every ref rewritten to an in-document pointer, transitively and once per target. What could not be reached keeps its `$ref` and is counted as an `external_ref` skip.
- **Import many files, or a whole folder.** The Import dialog read `dataTransfer.files[0]` and its file input carried no `multiple`, so dropping a folder's contents imported the first file and discarded the rest without a word - in the one subsystem that tallies every item it cannot represent. Entry is per file now: mixed formats in one batch work by construction, the preview becomes a ledger with a row for every picked file (parsed, unrecognised, unreadable, or inlined into another document as a `$ref` target), and Apply is one call per file so a refused seventh cannot roll back six good ones. Vendors shipping one spec per service are the norm - PayPal's public surface is 13 documents in one folder.
- **Load runs can consume SSE.** `POST /runs` takes `stream: true`, reading the flag and its two caps through the same parser `POST /execute` uses. A stream under load is bounded by construction - the loop refills concurrency per completion, so both caps are always set from the payload or the settings with no zero-means-unbounded spelling, and reaching either is a successful completion. The report gains a `stream` section: the per-completion event distribution, the totals, a derived events/sec and whether a cap was hit, absent for every run that did not stream.
- **A sampled streaming capture carries its events.** A post-request script asserting on `pm.response.events` passed in design mode and silently read `undefined` when replayed over load samples - the same script, two behaviours. The events are now rebuilt from the stored body by the same parser the live path feeds, so what counts as an event has one definition, and both sampled-capture viewers render a streamed sample's timeline.
- **Send one request with one data row.** A pre-request script reading `pm.iterationData`, or a URL carrying `{{data.id}}`, needed a whole collection run per line of script to test. A caret on Send now lists the collection's data rows and sends bound to one, with both scripts reading the row as `pm.iterationData` at iteration 0 of 1. The row binds before the run row exists, so a refusal leaves no trace of an execution that never happened; a streaming send binds it too. `run_request` over MCP takes the same field, and its allowlist gate is now positional about templates - one in the path or query leaves the host knowable and is judged on that host.
- **`{{data.*}}` in auth credentials on a single send.** A credentials file is the canonical data-driven run, yet the token worked under Run collection and was refused under Send-with-row, the surface built for iterating on exactly that request. `build_request` now takes an auth resolution, so a caller that must reach the credentials first says so instead of hiding the `auth` key, and the join-then-apply is shared with the plan path rather than existing in two spellings. Percent-encoding an api key and base64-ing basic auth stay after the bind, which is the whole point of the ordering. OAuth 2.0 stays refused, narrowed to that mode: its token is acquired against the token endpoint, so no row can reach it.
- **Save a live response as an example, and delete one.** Examples could only be grown by re-importing a collection or hand-curling the engine's CRUD routes, though every piece of the loop existed already - the response is on screen, the request is saved, and the mock serves the first ordered example per route. A "Save as example" action sits at the right of the response tab strip because it acts on the whole exchange, and `request_examples` gains an `origin` column so a user-saved example is never handed to the next spec sync to overwrite. The Examples panel gains delete: an example you can create and never remove is a zombie.

### Changed

- **A `Set-Cookie` no longer follows a redirect across origins.** The vcpkg baseline moved from June to August, which carries curl 8.20.0 to 8.21.0 and with it upstream's "don't pass on set cookies to new origins". The engine sets `CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION` per request on all three transfer paths, so the change reaches design mode, the load event loop and SSE streams alike - a login that bounces through an identity provider on another host is the case to check. curl is the security-relevant half of the bump: curl.se lists 18 vulnerabilities whose last-affected release is 8.20.0, and the pin was the only thing holding them. cpp-httplib moves seven minors, openssl, sqlite3, gtest, nghttp2 and valijson each move a point release, and the baseline now has an owner: the release window is the cadence, and a bump lands as its own PR before the release commit.
- **The engine settings tree got its shelves fixed.** One knob had two editors: `liveReplayWindowMs` rendered as "Live Chart Window" in the engine list with a staged Save bar and as "Chart window" under App > Dashboard with autosave buttons, so staging one while flipping the other left a staged row showing a value nobody saved there. The Dashboard row is now the only editor, and the pairing is written in one place both the renderer and the search index read. Observability & Data held 24 of 48 entries and split into Observability and Data & retention; a new Services category holds the webhook inbox and SSE caps, matching the Dock drawer; "General & Engine" becomes "Core" (it sat under a heading already reading "Engine Settings"). A seeded category the renderer does not declare drops its entry from the search index and renders it nowhere, so the two lists are now pinned against each other with an alarm for a category becoming a dumping ground.
- **A restored response says what the live one did.** The trace stored only the *composed* header map, which the response pane then labelled as sent - so after a reload the panel listed a value-less header libcurl dropped and a `form-data` Content-Type libcurl rewrote, and was missing the body-implied Content-Type and default User-Agent the live panel showed. The sent record now rides the trace beside the composed map, written from the very appends that build libcurl's header list.
- **A load run's start concurrency is refused below 1 inline.** The engine has rejected it with a 400 since `validate_run_config` landed, but `min={1}` on a controlled number input is advisory and clearing the field reads back as `Number("") === 0`, so the only feedback arrived after Start. Ramp-Up and Capacity Discovery now get the blocking notice their three siblings had, refusing the value rather than silently raising it.

### Fixed

- **A `{{data.*}}` value bound into an XML body is escaped for the part it lands in.** `Ben & Jerry's` made the document malformed and `</customer><injected/><customer>` changed its shape, both silently, both surfacing only as the origin's 400. XML has no single escape set the way a JSON string literal does, so the rule reads the token's position: character data escapes `&`, `<` and `>`; an attribute value escapes the quote in force; a CDATA section stays verbatim with a `]]>` split across a reopened section. A comment or a processing instruction gets no encoding and is refused instead - a value carrying `-->` or `?>` would end the construct and send a document nobody wrote.
- **A value-less header is no longer reported as sent.** libcurl reads a header line with nothing after the colon as an instruction to *remove* the header, so an enabled row with an empty value never reached the wire on any transport while the sent-headers panel listed it. The panel exists to be trusted about what went out, so the record is corrected to match the wire rather than the other way round, and all three drivers now build the list and fill the record through one function - building them separately is how they drifted.
- **Optional value-less OpenAPI header parameters import disabled**, the rule v0.17.1 applied to query parameters and left headers out of. An operation declaring an optional `X-Request-Id` produced a Headers table claiming to send it with nothing in it. `required: true` stays enabled and a declared value imports enabled-with-value, by the same precedence; the row builder now serves both kinds rather than being copied, since a hand-rolled second copy would not receive the first's fixes.
- **A streaming Send allows `pm.sendRequest` like a buffered one does.** The same button allowed a script-issued request with the Event stream toggle off and refused it, pointing at a Settings control, with the toggle on - the renderer's payload was short a field the engine already reads before it branches on `stream`. The Settings tab's note that scripts cannot run on a stream is also gone: they can, and the note now says *when* they run, since Send answers as the stream opens and the Tests half runs once it has terminated.
- **A live stream at shutdown no longer crashes the daemon.** A consumer worker writes its run row through the database from inside its completion callback, which runs after the stream is already flagged closed, and nothing joined those workers before the database was torn down; a layer up, `curl_global_cleanup()` ran between stopping the server and destroying it, so a live stream was inside a transfer while curl's global state went away. Draining is now an explicit, terminal, idempotent step that `Server::stop()` calls once the listener is down, covered by tests that assert in plain builds rather than relying on a sanitizer - and a `linux-asan` preset lands with them.
- **A `{{data.email}}` token's tooltip can be opened, and script chips stop painting data columns red.** The variable overlay paints with `pointer-events: none` so clicks reach the input underneath; the runtime-token wrapper never re-enabled them, so the tooltip that is its entire content could never open. Re-enabling them costs the caret the click placed, so each token now carries its own offsets and a click lands the caret at the token's near edge - never between the braces, where a keystroke corrupts the name. The script panels' chip row read a working `data.*` column as undefined and painted it destructive; it reads the same describer the overlay does now, and the row is relabelled "Names mentioned", with `{{name}}` chips neutral because the engine never interpolates script source.
- **Send-with-row's remembered row stopped following you between request tabs.** The request builder is rendered at the same position for every tab and is not keyed, so a single `lastRowIndex` in its state carried the highlight and the one-click re-send target from one request to the next. It is keyed by request id now.
- **A saved example's truncation disclosure cannot be edited away.** A partial body was disclosed only by a suffix on the default *name*, a field the save dialog invites you to change. `request_examples.body_truncated` is a column now, and the Examples panel paints a "Partial body" chip; a mock still serves the stored bytes verbatim, since the flag is disclosure rather than behaviour.
- **Releases compile against a warm sccache again.** `DEFAULT_USER_AGENT` was `"Vayu/" VAYU_VERSION_STRING` in `core/constants.hpp`, a header ~every translation unit reaches transitively, so every version bump invalidated the whole compile cache and each release rebuilt from scratch on all three platforms. The symbol moved to a `core/user_agent.hpp` that includes nothing.
- **`scripts/pre-commit` refuses loudly on clang-tidy < 19** instead of scanning an empty set and exiting clean - `engine/.clang-tidy` uses `ExcludeHeaderFilterRegex`, which 18 rejects, and Ubuntu 24.04 ships 18 by default. Exactly the shape of defect the non-empty-scan discipline exists to prevent.
- **16 engine tests that had never run once now do.** `response_capture_test.cpp` had been on disk since the load-run capture feature landed and was never listed in the test target, so the whole feature plus `GET /runs/:id/samples` went ~140 commits unexercised. Registering it turned up one aged assertion, fixed rather than deleted. A configure-time guard now fails the build naming any test file that is not registered, and an empty glob is itself a failure.

### Internal

- **A stale vcpkg clone heals itself.** A clone older than `builtin-baseline` fails every dependency with wording that reads as a corrupt tree, and the `git fetch` the error suggests cures the first message and exposes a second. Baseline bumps are routine by design, so every environment that has sat still meets this on its next build; `build.py` now brings the clone forward before installing dependencies and before configuring cmake, refuses to touch a modified checkout, and prints the manual cure wherever it cannot heal.
- The published site gains four Compare pages, a designed social card sized for the ratio the platforms crop against, and a real description on every page; the README is rewritten as the GitHub landing page rather than a second, staler copy of the install docs. The backlog file is retired in favour of the tracker, and the dashboard's five code-quality gates get a home in the repo instead of citing a document that was never committed.
